depth_findings.text: The birth stamp is a behaviour change for every user run (a new metadata write of origin=chat on each StartRun INSERT), and this slice declares no switch, so the 'byte-identical with switches off' rule does not hold for user runs; the owner should confirm the mandated default is acceptable before enabling.
The birth stamp (run_origin_at_birth) is covered only by a pure unit test; no DB test proves that a StartRun for a user lands metadata.origin=chat in runs, and that a system-owned run gets no stamp.

Nothing enforces the row's 'ZDR runs chat only' clause at the origin level: a ZDR run is refused by the scheduled-lane gates (Control decisions, RecordScheduledRunResult), not by the origin vocabulary itself.

The legacy-merge branch in persist_scheduled_run_bindings has no test for a stamp of JSON null on a scheduled run (today it is refused because Null reads as chat), and that edge should be decided explicitly.
The Go twin RunOriginFromMetadata and ParseRunOrigin have no production caller until S3/S7 land; the Go half is test-only for now.
Trigger and Api origins are in the closed set but no writer stamps them yet; the Space turn_origin mapping (owned by Space) is not built here.

The birth stamp (run_origin_at_birth in session-core grpc.rs) writes origin=chat into every user run's metadata with no switch, so user runs change behaviour on deploy; the row mandates the chat default, but the owner should confirm this as an unflagged change since the slice declares no flag.

The row's 'ZDR runs chat only' clause has no origin-level guard or test: persist_scheduled_run_bindings never checks runs.retention_class, and the clause holds only structurally (start_scheduled_run hard-codes RunRetention::persistent(), and Control refuses ZDR); add a refusal to stamp schedule when the run's retention is zdr or waived, with a test.

apps/Model Plane/rust/crates/mp-contracts/src/lib.rs (one line, pub mod run_origin;) is edited but absent from the slice's owned file list; the module cannot compile without it, so the lead should record it as an accepted ownership addition rather than treat it as a stray edit.
The Rust and Go origin tables are hand-copied known answers rather than the shared vector file the row names; a single shared fixture would make the twin pinning enforceable.

Runs not started through start_run for a person are unstamped and read as chat by absence: system-owned non-scheduled runs (start_run with no user) and managed delegation child runs (terminalization.rs insert_managed_run_started) get no stamp, and trigger and api have no writer, so origin reads wrong for these runs.

No DB test proves that a user StartRun lands metadata.origin=chat, or that a system-owned run gets no stamp; only the pure run_origin_is_stamped_at_birth_for_people_only unit test covers the birth path.

DEC-17's default to rename the other origins (skill, memory, turn) in wire and docs is not done, and the sse-event-taxonomy.md note is not added; the generated file needs a change through apps/Model Plane/scripts/gen-sse-event-taxonomy.py, not by hand.
A scheduled run stamped with a JSON null origin is refused by origin_bindable (Null reads as chat, so it is not Schedule); this is the conservative choice and is untested.

start_run_inner and persist_scheduled_run_bindings run in separate transactions, so a scheduled run row briefly carries metadata {} and reads as chat in that window; acceptable for a queued run but worth knowing.
The Go twin ParseRunOrigin and RunOriginFromMetadata have no production caller until S3/S7 land; they are test-only for now.

results.notes: Built the origin vocabulary and its stamping. mp-contracts::run_origin has the closed enum (chat, schedule, trigger, api), exact-match parse (unknown refused), and from_metadata (absent or null reads chat, non-token refused). The Go twin in capability-core models has the same table and a RunOriginFromMetadata helper, pinned by the same known answers. session-core: start_run_inner's INSERT now stamps metadata.origin=chat for non-system owners (run_origin_at_birth); system owners get no stamp. persist_scheduled_run_bindings stamps origin=schedule into a fresh run's metadata. A legacy run (exact binding, no stamp) takes the stamp by a jsonb merge that keeps every other key. A run stamped with any origin other than schedule is refused with the same permission_denied as a binding mismatch. The FE runs-client normalizer reads metadata.origin into an optional RunDetail.origin: absent gives chat, an unknown token gives undefined. No proto change, no migration, no switch (the batch declares none). Note the working tree of session-core grpc.rs and mp-contracts lib.rs also carries hunks from other sessions in this worktree; the lead must stage only the hunks listed in files_changed.
